pr_title: Add runtime field of type geo_shape
pr_body:
This PR adds the possibility to create runtime fields of type geo-shape. In order to create them, user s can define an emit function that takes either a geojson object or a WKT string that internally creates a geo_shape object. For example from a geo_shape doc value, we can generate the WKT representing the bounding box of the shape like (in yaml):

```
runtime:
              geometry_from_doc_value:
                type: geo_shape
                script:
                  source: |
                    GeoBoundingBox bbox = doc["geometry"].getBoundingBox();
                    emit("BBOX(" + bbox.topLeft().getLon() + "," + bbox.topLeft().getLat() + "," + bbox.bottomRight().getLon() + "," + bbox.bottomRight().getLat() + ")");
```

closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/61299
pr_comments: Hi @iverase, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: Runtime fields to support runtime type geo-shape
issue_context.body: As a follow-up of #59332, we'd like to add support for runtime fields that have `runtime_type` `geo-point` and `geo-shape`.
comments:
I work on Kibana maps team and have a customer asking for runtime geo_shape support. Below is the use case.

Customer has geo-locations that are not precise GPS positions but rather a location with an error ellipse. The error ellipse is stored as a center lat/lon, semi-minor axis length, semi-major axis length, and an origination from north. The error ellipse centers are indexed as geo_points in elasticsearch. Customer would like to use a runtime field to generate the error ellipse polygon from Elasticsearch vector tile search API.

review_comments: Is there perhaps value in testing something more than a point, perhaps a two point linestring?
Edit: ah no, if we have multiple geometries then they get wrapped into a GeometryCollection, ok.
I added a comment to clarify it
All these tests seem to test only points. I wonder if there is value in testing something a little more complex, perhaps at least a two point linestring?
I changed to run with a LINESTRING

I noticed these two versions of the constructor, but when looking up the constructor stack, I see they do ultimately end up at the same place, so I wonder if it is not cleaner to have a single constructor with just null for the script parts when missing? This would reduce code in several classes that have multiple constructors just for scripts.
The base class expect a different constructor to be used. This might be a nice follow up but not for this PR as it touches other mappings like geo_point.
Is this going to be a problem with concurrency?  We have a single `reader` object here for the whole query but we may call `matches` from multiple segment tasks in parallel.

good catch! I move the creation of the visitor to the matches. It will create one visitor for each call which is not great but compare to the cost of encoding the geometry, I don't think it is worthy to try to optimize it.
The visitor is fine as a top-level field, it's the `reader` that needs to be done per-call I think?
doh! yes the reader needs to be moved here but the visitor too, it holds a state when visited that is not thread safe.
Same comment as above that we could remove these extra constructors, I think.
